articleTitle: Passivity-Based Fractional-Order Sliding Mode Control for Fractional-Order Hyperchaotic Systems with Unknown Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper we investigate the problem of passivity-based sliding mode control for fractional-order hyperchaotic systems with unknown parameters. Utilizing the fractional calculus, the fractional-order sliding surface is chosen. The state trajectories of the closed-loop system reach the fractional-order sliding surface in finite time under the control of the designed controller. The control law ensures the asymptotical stability on the sliding surface. A parameter adjustment scheme for fractional-order integral sliding surface is proposed by using the linear matrix inequality approach. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for the synchronization control of fractional-order hyperchaotic systems with unknown parameters.

articleTitle: Coexisting Attractors with Nonlinear Offset-Boosting and Transient Chaos in a Memristive Complex-valued Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Due to the widespread application of memristors, it is of great significance to conduct in-depth research on the nonlinear dynamics of complex networks based on memristors. This article constructs a memristor-based complex-valued network. Although the network structure is simple, abundant dynamical behaviors have also been observed, including phenomena such as hyper-chaos and quasi-period. In addition, there is a transient chaotic phenomenon in the network. Moreover, multiple coexisting attractors are obtained, which exhibit the trend of nonlinear migration.

articleTitle: Memristor-based Mixed Training Scheme with Multi-level Sparsification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Memristor crossbar is naturally suit for the on-chip neuromorphic computing systems by its properties like non-volatile nature, low power consumption, and dense layout. However, cause the unmature manufacturing technology of the memristor, lots of problems are still exists in its practical application. One of the most significant problems is the network accuracy loss due to non-ideal characteristics of the device and crossbar. In this paper, we propose a mixed training scheme with multilevel sparsification to address this problem and also the operational complexity problem in network in-situ training. The scheme we proposed can minimize non-ideal characteristics effects and enables the network to maintain a high level of accuracy while greatly reducing the complexity of network training operations. Meanwhile, we fit the non-ideal characteristics of the device with the real experimental data, which highly reproduces the environment where the network in-situ training needed for better testing of our proposed scheme. The experiments show that the updating efficiency of the network is improved by almost 20% with the training accuracy is only reduced by about 8 % compared to the full-software training network, which fully proves the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Multistability and Hidden Attractors in a Fractional-Order Memristive Tabu Learning Neuron Model and Its Medical Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In order to simulate the transmission and processing of information with neurons, a memristor is used as a synapse, which has an electromagnetic induction effect. This paper proposed a fractional-order tabu learning neuron model with a memristor. Firstly, the analysis of the model's equilibrium points reveals the presence of hidden attractors. Secondly, the system is analyzed by bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponent diagrams and phase diagrams, which is found to have a rich dynamic behaviors. The attraction basins demonstrate that the system is characterized by multistability. Additionally, the two-parameter bifurcation diagram accurately provides a description of the system's firing behavior with different parameter values. Finally, Based on the chaotic sequence, this paper designed a novel medical image encryption algorithm. The reliability of this algorithm is then theoretically analyzed.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Tri-valued Memristors Based Ternary Data Selector Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: As a new type of nano-sized electronic component, memristor has the advantages of low power consumption, non-volatility and compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Especially, the circuits implemented by memristors has the function of in-situ storage and computation, which is considered to be a strong competitor for the continuation of Moore's Law. Traditional CMOS devices only have two states: open and closed, so most of the existing data selectors are designed based on binary logic. The appearance of ternary logic devices makes it possible to design data selectors based on ternary logic. In this paper, a design method of 9-to-1 data selector based on tri-valued memristors is proposed, which makes full use of the advantages of ternary logic that a single signal line carries more information and has low power consumption. The circuit can be realized using only a small number of tri-valued memristors and voltage-controlled switches. On this basis, the ternary 9-to-1 data selector is designed and optimized, and further applied to implement a lookup table and a ternary numerical comparator. This research provides a new idea for the subsequent development and application of ternary digital logic circuits based on tri-valued memristor.

articleTitle: Time-Sensitive Semantic Communication Using Dynamic Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Semantic communication aims to extract and trans-mit the semantic information of objects to greatly reduce the transmission of redundant information. This means that termi-nals need to deploy large and deep models to extract semantic features, which greatly exacerbates the computational overhead on the terminal. This prevents many time-sensitive scenarios, such as industrial IoT and vehicular networking, from achieving satisfactory QoS. To alleviate this issue, we propose a Time-Sensitive Semantic Communication paradigm (TSSC) that fulfills the latency requirements of the tasks by balancing the computational and communication overhead at the terminal. To achieve this purpose, we design a Dynamic Spiking Neural Networks (DSNNs). DSNNs can dynamically adjust the timing of semantic feature acquisition to meet the task's latency constraints. And DSNNs can be applied directly to digital channels, thus avoiding the quantization process. Furthermore, the leaky integrate and fire characteristics of DSNNs enable hardware acceleration on memristors to further reduce computing latency. Experiments demonstrate that DSNNs can be well adapted to TSSC tasks, which can achieve high accuracy in semantic communication tasks while maintaining low latency.

articleTitle: Chaos and Synchronization in a Memristor-Coupled HR-FN Neuron
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Artificial neural networks are commonly employed to mimic biological activities in the brain. Synapse as the neuron connecter plays an important role in information transmission, which revises the dynamics of coupled neurons inevitably or even bring synchronization behavior. In this work, by coupling the FitzHugh-Nagumo neuron (FN) and Hindmarsh-Rose neuron (HR) with a memristor synapse, a 5D neuron system is derived. The dynamics and synchronization feature of the coupled memristive neuron including period-doubling bifurcation and chaotic bursting were exhaustively studied through phase portraits, Lyapunov exponents, and bifurcation diagrams. It shows that the coupling strength of the synapse poses a great impact on the evolution of membrane potential including phase synchronization and complete synchronization. In addition, the derived HR-FN Neuron has the property of offset boosting and local frequency control. Offset boosting poses unique effects on synchronization when the derived neuron exhibits different firing dynamics.

articleTitle: A New Method for Predefined-Time Synchronization Control of Memristive Cohen-Grossberg Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: This article mainly conducts a series of research on the synchronization control of Cohen-Grossberg neural networks. Firstly, a memristive Cohen-Grossberg neural network model with time-varying delay was constructed, and an equivalent system was obtained by combining inverse function theory, differential inclusion, and set-valued mapping. Secondly, a new predefined-time stability theorem was proposed, and sufficient conditions were obtained to ensure that the drive-response system achieves predefined-time synchronization by designing appropriate control strategy. The simulation results show that the stability time of the error system can be adjusted by the user, verifying the correctness and of the theory.

articleTitle: When a Neuron and its Self-Cascade System Coupled by a Memristor Synapse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: The memristor can showcase the induced currents between neurons, serving as synapses that link two neural systems. At the same time, self-cascade operations yield new systems with original discrete dynamics. This paper proposes a hybrid construction method with coupling neuron system based on discrete memristor synapses and self-cascade operations. Rulkov and Chialvo neurons are employed as the foundation, and the coupled systems are analyzed. Two synchronous transitions are observed in the coupled system of Rulkov neurons, whereas new discharge patterns emerge in the hybrid coupling Chialvo neurons. The numerical simulations and theoretical analysis have been proved in the CH32 hardware platform.

articleTitle: Enhancing Mobile Game Performance with Hybrid Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: This research article addresses optimizing performance in 3D interactive applications, such as games, simulations, and augmented reality experiences, specifically on mobile devices. The study aims to overcome challenges related to suboptimal performance caused by code inefficiencies and memory mismanagement. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that combines Shadow Masking (SM) and Level of Detail (LOD) techniques in a synergistic manner, aiming to enhance performance while maintaining visual quality. We carefully analyze factors such as visual realism and computational overhead using tools like Unity3D and Blender, which provide physics simulations, audio integration, and photorealistic rendering capabilities. This analysis helps us determine the most effective SM and LOD strategies for specific game environments. Additionally, we develop a methodology using the Unity game engine and 3D models designed in Blender, resulting in a mobile 3D game environment optimized for smooth performance. This research introduces a novel approach to automatically recognize and remove shadows using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This aspect is particularly significant in mobile game development, where limited processing power, memory, and battery life pose unique challenges. Our insights aim to assist game developers in enhancing the player experience, even on mobile devices with lower specifications, by optimizing game environments while maintaining visual quality and performance.

articleTitle: A Full-Functional Pavlov Associative Memory Biomimetic Neural Circuit with Memcapacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Most associative memory neural networks have traditionally been implemented using memristors. However, memcapacitors, which are capable of simulating the biological behavior of neurons, exhibit characteristics that are often more advantageous than memristors in realizing pavlov associative memory neural networks. This article proposes a neural network architecture based on memcapacitors. Within this framework, we have successfully implemented five classical conditional reflex functions, including learning and forgetting, time interval conditioning, time delay conditioning and blocking. The design involves the interconnection of five similar neuron modules through various synapses. This memcapacitive biomimetic neural circuit not only offers a comprehensive platform for the realization of five classical conditional reflexes but also exhibits scalability.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Neural Network: Hidden Firing Patterns, Phase Synchronization and Multistability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel heterogeneous neural network is proposed by coupling improved memristor 2D HR neuron and 1D HNN neuron with locally active memristor. The effect of coupling intensity on synchronization behavior is analyzed. The results show that the increase in coupling intensity will lead to phase synchronization of the system. The coexistence of the firing pattern caused by the initial enhancement of the memristor is quantitatively analyzed and numerically simulated by introducing a multistable auto memristor. The results show that the newly constructed heterogeneous neural network exhibits an attractor bias pattern that enhances the initial migration behavior of the memristor, and these patterns have extreme multi-stability.

articleTitle: Analysis of Attractor Growing of Memristor in FitzHugh-Nagumo Neuron
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel three-dimensional FHN (FitzHugh-Nagumo model) neuron model incorporating a memristor, which is an improvement derived from adding a sinusoidal magnetic conductive memory to the existing FHN neuron model. Employing the ODE45 algorithm, we utilize Lyapunov exponents and bifurcation plots to analyze neuronal activity under different parameters and demonstrate that the improved three-dimensional FHN neuron model with memristor exhibits certain chaotic phenomena under specific conditions. Through the inference analysis of the offset mechanism of the new neuronal model, it is found that it has hidden infinite number of firing modes coexisting. In addition, it has been found that it also has a chaotic attractor growth phenomenon.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Memristive Bursting Networks with Super Multistability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: As a signal triggering and transmission mode in nervous systems, bursting plays an important role in the coding and transmission of neural signals. Theoretical analysis and applications of the network constructed by memristor synapse is of great significance. Bursting vibration and the corresponding super multistability in a simplest memristor-based network are discovered, and the trigger mechanism of the bursting is clarified, and the super multistability is numerically analyzed. Finally, the physical circuit is constructed and implemented, verifying the above theoretical and numerical analysis. The discovery stretches the understanding of dynamic behaviors of memristor networks.

articleTitle: Dynamics Analysis of Fractional-Order Memristive Neural Network and Its Application in Military Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: The chaotic signals generated by the memristive neuron system provide high security, which is important for image encryption. In this paper, a fractional-order memristive neuron network system is proposed. The system has a symmetric coexistence behavior through numerical simulations. Moreover, including an external current in this neuronal network model can generate bursting behavior. Due to the high security of chaotic sequences generated by the neuronal network system. A new military image encryption scheme is proposed using fractional order memristive neuron system and hash function. The results are analyzed through security tests, which show that the proposed encryption scheme provides excellent security performance for military image communication.

articleTitle: A New Class of Sine-Cosine Chaotic Systems and Its Application to Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Considering the chaotic system can produce sequences with good pseudo-randomness and has a comprehensive application to image encryption, we propose a new class of sine-cosine chaotic systems and corresponding encryption scheme. Firstly, a new class of discrete chaotic systems based on sine and cosine functions is proposed. Taking two-dimensional chaotic system as an example, the phase diagram, time domain diagram, bifurcation diagram and Lyapunov exponents diagram of the system are drawn to verify the performance of the systems. Secondly, we design an image encryption algorithm. Finally, the simulation results show that the information entropy of the algorithm is close to the ideal value, and it can resist clipping and noise attacks, which verifies that the sine-cosine chaotic system has good cryptographic and pseudo-randomness characteristics.

articleTitle: Extreme Multistability with Offset Boosting of A Memristor-coupled Complex-valued Ring Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, a non-volatile memristor is introduced to construct a complex-valued ring network (CVRN) with three laser systems. It is found that there are two groups of equilibrium points when the parameters are special. Through the analyses of the system parameter and coupling parameter by bifurcation diagram and Lyapunov exponent spectrum, it is found that system has different states, including chaos, hyperchaos, and quasi-period. It appears the coexistence of two heterogeneous attractors, including a quasi-periodic attractor and a chaotic attractor, caused by a pair of symmetric initial values. More importantly, the change of memristor initial values leads to extreme multistability with offset boosting.

articleTitle: Exponentially Synchronization Control of Memristive Neural Network with fractional Brownian Motion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of exponential synchronous control of a memristive neural network with fractional Brownian motion(fBm). Based on the prevalent power law phenomenon in the nervous system and the same properties of memristor and neurons in the human brain, we consider the fBm as stochastic perturbation and use memristor to simulate biological synapses simultaneously to form a novel kind of memristor-based neural networks with random noise (SMNNs). Then, using the theory of stochastic differential equation with fBm and the infinitesimal generator principle, we obtained a sufficient condition for exponential synchronisation of memristive neural network with fBm. Numerical calculations validated the SMNNs with fBm.

articleTitle: A Novel Discrete Memristive Chaotic Rulkov Neuron Model with Electromagnetic Radiation and its Application in Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Discrete memristor can simulate the electromagnetic induction effect of discrete neuron, which is important for neurological research. In this paper, a discrete memristor with cosine memristance is constructed firstly, then a memristive chaotic Rulkov (MC-Rolkov) neuron model with electromagnetic radiation effect is proposed. The complex dynamics is numerically studied by bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponential (LE) spectrum and phase diagrams. The MC-Rolkov neuron model can generate self-growing chaotic attractors with sophisticated topological structures. Meanwhile, extreme multistability and transient chaotic attractors are found under some system parameters. Especially, the proposed MC-Rolkov neuron model can generate complex chaotic bursting behaviors. Finally, based on the MC-Rolkov neuron model, a new image encryption scheme is proposed, and the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has excellent security characteristics.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of DRAM NBTI Issues and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: A comprehensive review of NBTI issues and their preventions were summarized over the past years. The NBTI related process issues, degradation mechanism, and process solution were systemically summarized. We also analyzed some NBTI risk circuits and provided improve suggestions to enlarge DRAM circuit NBTI tolerance. To disclosure the circuit level real risk, a new methodology was investigated with quiz-static DC stress on ring oscillator. Its degradation exhibits a good corelation to that of single device level NBTI performance, and can be used to guide the definition of NBTI specification. This work provides some valuable insights to DRAM NBTI solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Memristive Hyperchaotic Image Encryption Experimental Platform Based on Embedded Linux System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this manuscript, an image encryption experimental platform based on hyperchaotic pseudo-random sequence is developed based on Linux operating system. The platform utilizes hyperchaotic synchronization technology for secure key transmission between encryption and decryption terminals. Firstly, a hyperchaotic system based on a tri-valued memristor is proposed. Then, the software of client and server are designed to realize the interactive transmission of images under different systems. Simultaneously, a network channel is constructed for file transmission. After that, the graphical user interface is designed based on QT tool, which ensures that the image encryption software possesses satisfactory visual effect and operability. Finally, encryption and decryption functions are developed in Linux system utilizing OpenCV library functions for image data handling. The results demonstrate that the platform effectively performs both image encryption and decryption functions, enhancing the security of embedded device information.

articleTitle: Stabilization for a Class of Switched Chaotic Systems via Arbitrary Switching
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Based on linear state feedback, a novel approach on how to control complex chaos generated from a class of switched chaotic systems via arbitrary switching is put forward. According to structural characteristics of each subsystem, linear state feedback controllers are designed to guarantee controlled switched chaotic systems degenerate into switched linear systems rapidly. By utilizing common quadratic Lyapunov function technique, the closed-loop systems are globally asymptotically stable at the origin under the condition of arbitrary switching. A numerical example verifies the effectiveness of the presented novel approach in this paper.

articleTitle: Dynamics Analysis and Projective Synchronization of a Novel Fractional-Order System and Application in Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Fractional-order system attracted researcher's attention due to the complicated behaviors and memory properties. To further investigate the dynamics of a fractional-order system and its application, a fractional-order system with a memristor is constructed based on the Sprott E system. The dynamics of the addressed system is studied, and projective synchronization is realized by designing controllers. Numerical simulations verify the theoretical results. Furthermore, according to the projective synchronization of the proposed systems, an image encryption algorithm is put forward and its effectiveness is analyzed from various aspects. By contrast with scrambling diffusion encryption algorithm, the addressed encryption algorithm shows certain advantages, because it makes full use of the characteristics of projective synchronization of chaos systems and can resist exhaustive attacks effectively.

articleTitle: Dynamics and information modulation in the Chialvo neuron networks with fractional-order discrete memristor coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: At present, design and dynamics analysis of neuron networks are becoming a topic worthy of further study, in which the couple controller has been widely applied. In this paper, we designed a ring coupled neuron network with Chialvo neurons and fractional-order discrete memristor coupling. Thus the input of memristor is the state variable difference of the two nearby neurons and the output become to be the control signal. According to the numerical simulations, it shows that the neuron network has rich dynamics and there exists chaos. Meanwhile, chimera states and multistatbility are found in the network. It shows that the collective behaviours are different with different initial conditions. In conclusion, it indicates that the network can store some information according to the behaviours of the network and initial conditions.

articleTitle: Multi-scroll, Extreme Multi-stability, and Phase Synchronization Phenomena of Memristor-based Complex-valued Chain Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, based on the complex-valued Lorenz system, a new system is obtained by introducing multi-stable memristor to the three-node chain network. First, we study the rich dynamics of the system, and find the inverse period-doubling bifurcation, hyper-chaotic and quasi-periodic attractors. The emergence of multi-scroll attractors is an interesting phenomenon in this paper, and different scroll numbers can appear by adjusting the parameters. The extreme multi-stability of the system is another focus of this paper, and the variation of the initial value of the system induces coexisting behavior such as the offset boosting of the attractor. Finally, the synchronization of the network is studied.

articleTitle: Design of Handwritten Recognition System based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Handwritten digit recognition is essential for the usage of smart devices and modern applications. It has become one of the important problems in the field of machine vision and received massive attention from both industry and academia in deep learning area. In this paper, we focus on the design and implementation of handwritten recognition system based on convolutional neural network (CNN). We give out the structural design of our system and then report each key component of it. Specifically, it takes pictures with handwritten digits as input, and then goes through a series of image processing steps, including gray scale, binarization, color reversal, noise reduction, segmentation, and size normalization, and finally realizes the automatic recognition and classification, i.e., the results of handwritten digits. We also conduct a series of experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our system.

articleTitle: Finding Coexisting and Multi-Cavity Chaotic Attractors in Memristor-Based Hénon Map
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Although memristors are widely utilized in continuous chaotic systems, research into discrete memristive systems has been relatively limited. This paper introduces a novel three-dimensional discrete chaotic map by incorporating a sinusoidal memristor model into the classical Hénon map. In contrast to prior memristor-based Hénon maps, the proposed system not only generates hidden coexisting attractors but also exhibits an infinite number of multi-cavity chaotic attractors, which is seldom seen among existing systems. Numerical simulations, including Lyapunov exponents(LEs), bifurcation diagrams, and phase diagrams, are provided to investigate parameter-dependent dynamics. Both initial-boosted coexisting attractors and the multi-cavity chaotic attractors can be found by setting appropriate parameters. This research contributes to a better understanding of chaotic phenomena and promotes the development of discrete memristive chaotic systems.

articleTitle: Adjusted and Controllability Properties of Memristor Rucklidge System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: There are many models of memristors, but there are no reports on exponential memristors. In this paper, a three- dimension memristor Rucklidge system with exponential memristor is proposed by introducing exponential function and constructing exponential memristor. The dynamic behavior of the system is analyzed by means of Lyapunov exponent and bifurcation diagram. The complex attractor coexistence and amplitude modulation characteristics of the system are found. The internal variable of memristor is introduced into the second two-dimensional equation as a feedback term, and a conditional symmetric system is constructed for the three-dimensional memristor system, which can realize the polarity control of output signal. By discussing the dynamic characteristics of exponential memristor chaotic system and the control mechanism of amplitude modulation, bias and conditional symmetry, the complex dynamic characteristics of exponential function memristor are revealed, which lays a foundation for its application in the field of secure communication.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Enabled Fault Detection Method for RRAM-Based Neural Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In the era of big data and advanced computing, a constant escalation in the demand for computational power is observed. This paper addresses the challenges in current computing architectures, with a specific focus on the inefficiencies of the von Neumann architecture and the limitations inherent in Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM). A novel Digital Twin Enabled Fault Detection Method for RRAM-Based Neural Com-puting Systems is introduced. This method utilizes Digital Twin technology to bridge the physical and digital realms, enabling the creation of precise virtual models of RRAM devices for simulation and analysis without physical risks. The framework of the system, its construction methodology, and experimental results are detailed. Enhanced reliability of RRAM devices is achieved through this approach by facilitating predictive maintenance and early fault detection, thereby reducing unexpected downtimes in various applications.

articleTitle: A Memristive Chaotic 5D System With 3D Offset Boosting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this article, a 5D memristive chaotic system with three 3D offset boosting is designed and analyzed. By introducing three independent offset constants in the system equation, different regimes of offset boosting are defined by the external constants including various combinations of reverse control and differential control. Furthermore, the offset boosting is also influenced by the coefficient of the linear terms, which is a bifurcation parameter. Finally, the memristive 5D chaotic circuit is designed based on the software of Multisim. Circuit simulation validates the function of offset boosting from the separated three constants.

articleTitle: Dynamics of a Nonlinear System with Multiple Coexisting Attractors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: A new nonlinear system is derived in this paper. The nonlinear system has three nonlinearities including a hyperbolic tangent function, a sine function and a quadratic function. The system has infinite equilibria located a hyperbola. Different shaped attractors can be generated from the system under different initial conditions. Moreover, the nonlinear system can also generate multiple coexisting attractors with different sizes.

articleTitle: Spiking and Bursting Dynamics in a Memristive Complex-variable Laser Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this research, a two-node memristive laser network is created by building a non-volatile memristor to couple two heterogeneous laser systems. The neurodynamic behaviors emerging in the network are explored. When the dynamics in relation to parameters are examined, it is discovered that the line width enhancement factor has a major impact on neural behaviors, including spiking firings and bursting firings. Coexisting attractors and coexisting spiking firings have been identified in the study of initial-values-related bistability. Finally, in order to make the chaotic signal meet the requirements of engineering equipment, the chaotic attractor is rotated to control the polarity and amplitude.

articleTitle: Memristive Circuit Design of Operant Conditioning with Bridging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Most of the previous operant conditioning neural network circuits only consider the basic theory and ignore the effect of additional stimuli on operant conditioning, such as bridging stimulus. In this paper, a memristor-based operant conditioning circuit with bridging is designed. The designed circuit is mainly composed of delay module, voltage control module and experience module. The various processes of operant conditioning are taken into account. The designed circuit realizes the feedback learning, experience memory, experience-based decision making and bridging functions in operant conditioning. The effect of the length of the bridging stimulus on operant conditioning is also taken into account. The study of operant conditioning with bridging can provide a reference for the study of more intelligent brain-like systems.

articleTitle: A Memristive Chaotic System: Attractor Self-Reproducing, Amplitude Control and Offset Boosting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Two flux-controlled memristors sharing the same internal variable and the same resistor function are introduced into the simplest variable boostable system VB5 for constructing the 3-D memristive chaotic oscillator. The offset booster is well inherited from the original chaotic system for attractor boosting, which makes the corresponding oscillation controlled on different positions by a single offset constant. Meanwhile, the periodic resistor function makes attractors self-reproducing and produces infinitely many attractors under different initial conditions. Furthermore, the property of rotational symmetry implies an extra partial amplitude control. The amplitude of the system variables <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> signal can be modified by a single non-bifurcation parameter. Analog circuit simulation based on Pspice shows agreement with the theoretical and numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Circuit Based on Memristive Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Operant conditioning plays a pivotal role in the realm of biology and serves as a fundamental concept in the field of artificial intelligence reinforcement learning. While mem-ristive neural circuits related to operant conditioning have been explored, there is a dearth of research addressing the influence of various reinforcers and reinforcement methods on the learning process. This paper presents a novel operant conditioning neural network designed to learn using secondary reinforcers and spaced stimuli. It not only facilitates the acquisition of primary and secondary reinforcer learning but also investigates the disparate learning outcomes resulting from continuous reinforcement and interval reinforcement in operant conditioning. The proposed circuit's functionality is rigorously validated through PSPICE simulation, affirming its feasibility. This work provides an implementation idea for the hardware implementation of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Dynamical Analysis of a New Equation Inspired by a Floodlight Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Inspired by a model of a constant power floodlight, we present an interesting equation and give its dynamic analysis by mathematical tools and simulations. Firstly, the mathematical model of constant power floodlights is constructed. Then we find a flickering behavior under some condition and obtain the parameter range for stable operation. Finally, we find an interesting first order ordinary differential equation when the time constant in the above model is one, and discuss its characteristics. The mathematical analysis and simulations indicate it has special properties and will play a certain role in the design of sliding mode controllers.

articleTitle: Firing Patterns Transition and Multistability in an Autapse-Rulkov Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: The synaptic connection weight of neurons is variable, so memristors can be employed to mimic autapses. A discrete neuron model with a memristive synapse is constructed to explore the role of autapse in a single neuron. By numerical measures, complex dynamics behaviors of the neuron model are investigated, including firing pattern transition behaviors, multistability, and hyperchaotic firing behaviors, which have a tight connection to the parameters of the memristor. In addition, the spiking and bursting sequences are acquired on a development board for a digital signal processor (DSP). Finally, experimental results verified the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Fractional-Order Hyperchaotic System Influenced by Memristor and Its Remote Sensing Image Encryption Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, based on a simple chaotic system with a smooth flux-controlled memristor, a fractional-order memristive hyperchaotic system with two nonlinear terms and infinitely many equilibrium points is constructed. Numerical analysis shows that the system has novel dynamic characteristics in which the memristor parameter control multiple types of attractors and control the attractor amplitude. At the same time, the existence of transient behaviors and the coexistence of attractors greatly increase the complexity of the system, which can be confirmed by analysis of the system complexity. Finally, the system is applied to remote sensing image encryption, and the excellent performance of the hyperchaotic memristive system is verified by histogram and correlation analysis.

articleTitle: Classification of Optical Character Recognition Based on Memristive Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Memristors, with their small size, high speed and low power consumption, are applied to tasks such as classification of neural networks with great results in terms of computation and storage. In this paper, we propose an optical character recognition classification method based on amnesic convolutional neural network, using the convolutional and fully connected layers of the convolutional neural network constructed based on the amnesic model. The PReLU activation function is also used to replace the ReLU activation function for optimisation. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the model measured using optical character recognition Rendered SST2 data set is 52.62%, compared with the convolutional neural network, the accuracy loss is only 2.74%; meanwhile, the influence of the failure rate and conductivity state in the amnesia non-ideal characteristics on the accuracy rate is analysed, which provides theoretical guidance for the future physical production.

articleTitle: A class of controllable chaotic oscillators with memory components in series or parallel
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Memory components, such as memristor, memin-ductor and memcapacitor, can be incorporated into a dynamic system for the construction of chaotic circuits due to their inherent nonlinear characteristics. Two models of memristor and meminductor are designed for chaos generation, and followingly two simple chaotic circuits are constructed via the connection of a memristor, a meminductor and a capacitor in serial and parallel. Partial amplitude control of chaos can be easily obtained in the proposed structure, and the serial circuit shows the direct offset boosting of a system variable. The accuracy of the system analysis was verified through the Multisim simulation.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerance Framework for Memristor based Binarized Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: The memristor crossbar provides a new hardware structure for binary neural networks computing, such as binary multi-layer perception and binary convolution neural networks, owing to its convenience in vector-matrix multiplication. However, memristors are prone to faults due to the immature fabrication process and non-ideal characteristics, i.e. stuck-at faults and variations, which seriously affects the calculation accuracy and thus limiting practical applications. To address above problems, a framework has been proposed for fault tolerance in memristor crossbars. We adopt position-aware training to tolerate SAFs, and further adjust the binary weights according to the impact of variation faults on network accuracy. Experiments are conducted on CIFAR10 datasets, and the results demonstrate that the proposed framework can significantly improve the recognition accuracy of the network under SAFs and variations situations.

articleTitle: A New Predefined Time Stability Theorem and its Application in Multi-Modal Memristive Neural Network Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: This article proposes a new predefined-time (PDT) stability theorem, which offers more evident advantages compared to previous predefined-time stability. Firstly, based on the limitations of existing PDT stability, this theorem relaxed the limitations of sufficient conditions, which fill the gap in the research on PDT stability. Secondly, the PDT synchronization of multi-modal memristive neural networks (MM-MNN) is analyzed by the usability of the new judgment theorem. A matching PDT controller is designed and sufficient synchronization control conditions is obtained by utilizing generalized Lyapunov functional method, set-valued mapping, inequality analysis technique and differential inclusion theory. Meanwhile, the topological characteristics of multi-modal neuron and its impact on network synchronization behavior are presented. Finally, we provide some confirmatory numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Math Model for Ag/TiOx/FTO Memristor with Positive Photoconductance Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: Memristors are extensively employed in neuromor-phic computing systems due to their notable advantages in nonvolatility, low power consumption, high density, and fast resistance switching. In recent years, considerable research ef-forts have been dedicated to modeling memristors with diverse structures and physical mechanisms. However, relatively fewer investigations have explored the coexistence of physical effects and resistance switching memory behaviors of memristors and their corresponding modeling approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive study on constructing a physical memristor model based on the Ag/TiOx/FTO memristor, which exhibits remarkable functionalities in optical signal sensing, information storage, and processing. Initially, the Ag/TiOx/FTO memristor is fabricated through the sol-gel method, and experimental results confirm the memristor's positive photoconductance (PPC) effect. Subsequently, an in-depth analysis of the internal principles of the memristor is conducted, facilitating the successful completion of its modeling. Moreover, based on the memristor model, a further artificial vision array is constructed, which accomplishes the functions of image perception, storage, and preprocessing, improving the efficiency and accuracy of subsequent tasks.

articleTitle: Dynamics and Complexity Analysis of A Fractional-order Financial Risk System Based on Adomian Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fractional-order financial risk system with one absolute function term. The Adomian decomposition method (ADM) is used to numerically solve the fractional-order financial risk system. Dynamical characteristics are analyzed and phase portraits, Lyapunov exponents and bifurcation diagrams are discussed. It is indicated that fractional-order financial risk system exhibits chaotic and stable behavior. Furthermore, complexity analysis and the 0–1 test are applied to comprehensively investigate the financial risk system. The plots of complexity analysis and the 0–1 test validate the results from the Lyapunov exponents and bifurcation diagrams. Numerical results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach described here.

articleTitle: Simulation and Chaos Prediction of Wind Power Generator Based on Memristive LSTM Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this paper, the Memristive Long Short-Term Memory (MLSTM) algorithm is used to predict the chaos of the wind turbine system. Firstly, the model of the permanent magnet synchronous wind turbine system is established. At the same time, the Adomian algorithm is used to solve the numerical solution of the fractional-order system and draw the phase diagram. In addition, the MLSTM is exploited by replacing the neural network weight algorithm, and it is applied to the speed prediction of wind turbine system. The simulation results show that the MLSTM can effectively realise the forecast, offer suggestions for the management of a wind turbine system, and lay the foundation for directly implementing the memristor bathymetry algorithm using a memristor hardware circuit.

articleTitle: Fast Finite-Time Adaptive Neural Control for Pure-Feedback Stochastic Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: In this article, we solve the fast finite-time stabilization as well as adaptive neural control design issues for a class uncertain stochastic nonlinear systems. By employing the mean value theorem, the pure-feedback form can be transformed into strict-feedback case. Firstly, a new fast finite-time control scheme is proposed in virtue of generalizing the fast finite-time adaptive control strategy for deterministic systems to the stochastic case. Next, a novel adaptive neural control strategy is developed to simultaneously deal with the stochastic nonlinear systems with completely unknown nonlinearities as well as the disturbances term. Then, stability analysis have been given based on a Jensen's inequality.

articleTitle: No-code MLOps Platform for Data Annotation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: The increasing demand for large-scale training data in deep learning models has underscored the significance of efficient data annotation. However, manual labeling remains a time-consuming and labor-intensive process. In this paper, we propose a No-code MLOps-based data annotation system that empowers non-developers to train and apply auto-labeling models seamlessly. The system supports various annotation types, including bounding boxes, keypoints, and 3D point clouds, enabling versatile applications. We present experiments on object detection, custom keypoint estimation, and 3D point cloud segmentation, demonstrating the system's effectiveness. Our contributions include a user-friendly platform, flexible annotation support, and interactive management features, marking a step towards democratizing data annotation.

articleTitle: Stabilization and complete synchronization of a new time-reversed system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Memristive Computing and Applications (ICMCA)
abstract: This paper investigates the stabilization and com-plete synchronization problems of a new time-reversed system. Firstly, the time-reversed system is transferred into a new system whose equilibrium point is origin by making a coordinate transformation, and two single input controllers are designed to stabilize such system. Secondly, a dynamic feedback single input controller is proposed and applied to realize the complete synchronization between two time-reversed system with different initial conditions. Finally, some numerical examples are provided to verify the effectiveness and the validity of the proposed results.
